reviews.review: Makes me feel like a hacker.

reviewing this with all achievements earned, i loved this game that much! however if you aren't into command based games this probably isnt for you.

this game is a lot of fun to play, i found myself getting sucked in for hours. even when i was tired i didn't want to shut down because simply digging through files is a lot of fun.

i don't want to spoil too much about the game, and i had very little issues with it! first, the good stuff:
the story is awesome
the puzzle solving felt very rewarding (example minor spoiler: [spoiler]when you lose your gui and have to work with the terminal was a lot of fun, i wish there had been more scenarios where this happened.[/spoiler]
banger ost

now my 2.5 issues with my experience
.5:
   a: for those who don't have previous command prompt knowledge, this game can be a bit confusing to learn. it's nothing 
      complex and the help commands do help, i just think the tutorial could do a lot more.
   b: for those of us who know our way around command prompt, i found myself trying to create files (not possible without 
      a weird workaround way of doing it [spoiler]downloading a file, replacing all the text in the file with "" 
      { replace "<text>" "" } then renaming the file to what you want with { mv <filename> <newfilename> }[/spoiler]. you also 
      cant make folders to store files, you can only use the default folders you are given. not that this is a game where you
      are meant to keep all the files you find, but it was a shame i had to cram everything i wanted to keep (even if pointless) 
      into the two folders in /home.
1: the node map is horrendous to use in the mid to late game, and as far as i could find, there's no way to reorganize it without tampering with the actual game files.
2: during the final set of missions it is super easy to accidentally work ahead of what the game wants, and you end up getting stuck, having to backtrack and then return to (near) where you got stuck to continue. this was  a minor annoyance and the only time i had to pull up a guide for this game

despite these pretty minor flaws ([spoiler]i know i had more words for the flaws then i did for what i enjoyed, i just didn't want to spoil the good stuff like i said[/spoiler]) i still think the game is incredible fun, and if your looking for a shortish game to pass the time (around 10 hours) this is a steal for 10 bones.

Prototype for this game was created in 48 hours, the game subsequently developed over the course of the following three years and I must say - it's a brilliant title. Rich story (to me) and something I was pleasantly surprised with.

Wow... I just finished it and especially the Labyrinths DLC (Kaguya trails) was very nice. The original game felt more quicker, whereas in the Kaguya missions, you actually had to dig deeper and make use of your tools in situations where it is not obvious. Both endgames were very nice and adrenalin-rushy and the whole game was accompanied with good music scores who supported the vibe of the missions.

Spoiler alert, but very noteworthy remark about Labyrinth DLC:
[spoiler] There was a unique time in the Labyrinth DLC where the game takes place on your actual computer and the actual windows CMD (and not in the simulated environment!). How cool is that?! I have never seen that before! [/spoiler]

It has been a long time since I really enjoyed a game and I learnt more about hacking too. This game inspired me to go out and look into Grey Hack, which is a bit more realistic than this. However, Hacknet does teach you some core mechanics of hacking and moving around with the bash terminal. The terminal doesn't have many commands though, and some functions are used in a simpler manner like nmap. There is also not a easy way to edit .txt with leafpad or nano. That doesn't exist. So you have to use 'replace list,txt x y' and append. As far as I know there is not even a way to delete a line.

In short: Nice game that teaches some basics about the terminal and hacking, good music, adrenalin rushes, a bit repetitive missions, not many commands available, a bit of a weird ai with the email and netmap, but really fun to have played!

Just beat the base game, wanted to give my opinion on it

Hacknet has an engaging story, really excellent mechanics and funny writing, there are even references to real world UNIX software like WINE (a compatibility layer for UNIX)
It's not a particularly long game but if you take the time to read everything it can be a lot longer. 

Now for one or two nitpicks
A lot of the game revolves around "executables" and dll (dynamic link libraries), now the thing is dlls and exes are exclusive to windows and not other platforms unless you run them through a compatibility layer like WINE, which could be excused because of WINE's involvement in the story but at a certain point you deploy a dll on an embedded system, which wouldn't make sense to have WINE installed

At another moment in the game you lose the ability to see your graphical user interface for a while and unless you were following along can make it tricky to navigate

but besides those extremely detailed nitpicks it's an excellent game that if you have the dedication is well enjoyable

I really just want to say thank you for this. Truly. This was an absolutely fantastic experience and I fully enjoyed it all of the way through!

Not only was it challenging but it was fun to learn the syntax and skills required to progress.  Loved the flexibility, choices, and problem solving with just the right amount of help provided on the library servers. By the end I was moving quick on the keyboard and developed a huge sense of satisfaction when I got good at multitasking with the hack tools!

The ending was beautiful as well. I'd never give it away to those who haven't completed the game but the best way I can describe the end is elegant, sad, and even reflectively meaningful. Seriously, that was well worth the effort. You developed an overall amazing game and I'm looking forward to playing it again with less restraint just to see what happens.

Ugly to look at, irritating to progress, repetitive gameplay, uninspired quests; but all hidden under the "shell" of realism. I know 'realism' is the point, but this realism is more like if Guitar Hero had 132 buttons (6 strings x 22 frets) instead of 5 -- at that point, I might as well play an actual guitar, cause I can take that skill outside of the constraints of the game (shoutout to Rocksmith). Such a game only uses the excuse of 'realism' to pretend that it is beyond criticism, despite its blatant flaws -- Hacknet relies on you falling for that excuse to let it off the hook for being a bad game.
